## What is E2B?\
  
[Permalink: What is E2B?](https://github.com/e2b-dev/e2b#what-is-e2b)  
  
[E2B](https://e2b.dev/?utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=readme&utm_content=E2B) is an open-source infrastructure that allows you to run AI-generated code in secure isolated sandboxes in the cloud.

## Run your first Sandbox\
### 1. Install SDK\
```\
npm i e2b\
```\
\
Python\
\
```\
pip install e2b\
```\
\
### 2\. Get your E2B API key\
\
[Permalink: 2. Get your E2B API key](https://github.com/e2b-dev/e2b#2-get-your-e2b-api-key)\
\
1. Sign up to E2B [here](https://e2b.dev/?utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=readme&utm_content=E2B).\
2. Get your API key [here](https://e2b.dev/dashboard?tab=keys&utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=readme&utm_content=E2B).\
3. Set environment variable with your API key\
\
```\
E2B_API_KEY=e2b_***\
```\
\
### 3\. Start a sandbox and run commands\
\
[Permalink: 3. Start a sandbox and run commands](https://github.com/e2b-dev/e2b#3-start-a-sandbox-and-run-commands)\
\
JavaScript / TypeScript\
\
```\
import Sandbox from 'e2b'\
\
const sandbox = await Sandbox.create()\
const result = await sandbox.commands.run('echo "Hello from E2B!"')\
console.log(result.stdout) // Hello from E2B!\
```\
\
Python\
\
```\
from e2b import Sandbox\
\
with Sandbox.create() as sandbox:\
    result = sandbox.commands.run('echo "Hello from E2B!"')\
    print(result.stdout)  # Hello from E2B!\
```\
\
### 4\. Code execution with Code Interpreter\
\
[Permalink: 4. Code execution with Code Interpreter](https://github.com/e2b-dev/e2b#4-code-execution-with-code-interpreter)\
\
If you need to execute code with [`runCode()`](https://e2b.dev/docs/code-interpreting?utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=readme&utm_content=E2B)/ [`run_code()`](https://e2b.dev/docs/code-interpreting?utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=readme&utm_content=E2B), install the [Code Interpreter SDK](https://github.com/e2b-dev/code-interpreter):\
\
```\
npm i @e2b/code-interpreter  # JavaScript/TypeScript\
pip install e2b-code-interpreter  # Python\
```\
\
```\
import { Sandbox } from '@e2b/code-interpreter'\
\
const sandbox = await Sandbox.create()\
const execution = await sandbox.runCode('x = 1; x += 1; x')\
console.log(execution.text)  // outputs 2\
```\
\
### 5\. Check docs\
\
[Permalink: 5. Check docs](https://github.com/e2b-dev/e2b#5-check-docs)\
\
Visit [E2B documentation](https://e2b.dev/docs?utm_source=github&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=readme&utm_content=E2B).\
\
### 6\. E2B cookbook\
\
[Permalink: 6. E2B cookbook](https://github.com/e2b-dev/e2b#6-e2b-cookbook)\
\
Visit our [Cookbook](https://github.com/e2b-dev/e2b-cookbook/tree/main) to get inspired by examples with different LLMs and AI frameworks.\
\
## Self-hosting\
\
[Permalink: Self-hosting](https://github.com/e2b-dev/e2b#self-hosting)\
\
Read the [self-hosting guide](https://github.com/e2b-dev/infra/blob/main/self-host.md) to learn how to set up the [E2B infrastructure](https://github.com/e2b-dev/infra) on your own. The infrastructure is deployed using Terraform.\
\
Supported cloud providers:\
\
- 🟢 AWS\
- 🟢 Google Cloud (GCP)\
- [ ]  Azure\
- [ ]  General Linux machine\

E2B cloud sandbox is a secure and isolated cloud environment.The sandbox allows you to:

- Access Linux OS
- Create, list, and delete files and directories
- Run commands
- Run isolated code
- Access the internet

## Overview

# E2B SDK MCP Server

The E2B SDK MCP server is a code execution backend for AI assistants that runs AI-generated code inside secure Firecracker microVMs with ~150ms cold starts and hardware-level isolation. Built by [e2b-dev](https://github.com/e2b-dev) (Apache-2.0), it supports Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, R, Java, and Bash. The MCP server variant adds sandbox creation and code execution directly to MCP-compatible clients like Claude Desktop.

**TL;DR:** AI-generated code needs isolated execution environments, but local Docker containers lack hardware-level isolation and break down at scale. E2B solves this with Firecracker microVM-based sandboxing: sub-200ms cold starts, per-sandbox Linux kernels, and automatic teardown. With 11.1k GitHub stars and adoption by Perplexity, Cursor, and Vercel, E2B has become the standard execution substrate for AI agents.

## What Is E2B SDK?

E2B SDK is an open-source infrastructure platform for running untrusted, AI-generated code in cloud-isolated environments. Each sandbox runs as a dedicated Firecracker microVM with its own Linux kernel; each sandbox gets hardware-level isolation, not container-based separation. According to the [E2B GitHub repository](https://github.com/e2b-dev/E2B), the platform is fully LLM-agnostic: it works with OpenAI, Anthropic, Llama, Mistral, or any custom model.

The [E2B MCP server](https://github.com/e2b-dev/mcp-server) wraps this infrastructure into three core tools:

- `Sandbox.create`: Spin up a new isolated cloud environment
- `sandbox.runCode`: Execute code via the JavaScript/TypeScript SDK
- `sandbox.run_code`: Execute code via the Python SDK

The Code Interpreter SDK layer adds a Jupyter Server inside each sandbox, making execution stateful: variables persist between calls.

With 11.1k stars on GitHub and production adoption by companies including Perplexity, Cursor, Vercel, and Manus (per [E2B's LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/the-agent-times_aiagents-e2b-infrastructure-activity-7429643119983480832-71qS)), E2B has become a standard execution substrate for AI agent workflows.

## Use Cases

**AI code interpreters with iterative debugging.** The core loop: generate code, execute the code, observe results, refine. As [Firecrawl's MCP analysis](https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/best-mcp-servers-for-developers) notes, an AI that can write code is fundamentally different from one that can run it, check the output, and iterate. E2B closes that gap by running each iteration in an isolated sandbox. Augment Code's Context Engine accelerates this loop by resolving semantic dependencies before generation, reducing failed iterations.

**Data analysis assistants.** Upload a CSV, ask your AI assistant to analyze it, and E2B executes the generated pandas/matplotlib code server-side. The SDK automatically extracts chart data from Matplotlib, Seaborn, or Plotly outputs per [E2B's Codestral guide](https://e2b.dev/blog/guide-ai-code-execution-with-mistrals-codestral). For workflows needing database access, the [Prisma MCP Server](https://www.augmentcode.com/mcp/prisma) complements E2B's execution.

**Pre-production verification of migration scripts.** Per [Firecrawl](https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/best-mcp-servers-for-developers), E2B is "particularly valuable for data analysis, migration scripts, and any task where you want to verify logic before committing to it." Teams using [AWS Labs MCP Servers](https://www.augmentcode.com/mcp/awslabs-mcp) can pair E2B sandboxes to test generated infrastructure scripts before deployment.

**Autonomous coding agents.** Multi-agent frameworks like LangChain, AutoGen, and CrewAI need execution environments that scale independently of the host machine. Per [E2B's AutoGen integration blog](https://www.e2b.dev/blog/community-contribution-autogen-code-interpreter-with-e2b), "by default, AutoGen agents do the code execution locally via Docker which can be limiting for some use cases or possess some risks." E2B replaces local Docker execution with cloud-isolated microVMs. For broader agent tool orchestration, the [Composio MCP Server](https://www.augmentcode.com/mcp/composio) handles authentication across 100+ services. Augment Code's Context Engine resolves semantic dependencies across 400,000+ files, ensuring cross-file imports are accurately mapped before code reaches E2B execution, reducing iteration cycles for autonomous agents working across large codebases.

## Comparison

- **E2B:** Best for AI agent sandboxing and MCP integration. ~150ms cold start, Firecracker microVM isolation, no GPU support.
- **Modal:** Best for GPU-dependent ML workloads. Higher cold start, gVisor container isolation, supports H100, A100, and L40S GPUs.
- **Fly.io Sprites:** Best for long-running stateful agents. Similar cold start to E2B, Firecracker microVM isolation, GPU support not documented.
- **AWS Lambda:** Best for event-driven workloads within existing AWS infrastructure. ~150ms cold start, Firecracker microVM isolation, no GPU support.
- **Self-hosted (SkyPilot):** Best for cost optimization at scale. Cold start varies, full control over isolation, GPU support available.

Controlled benchmarks from [SkyPilot](https://blog.skypilot.co/skypilot-llm-sandbox/) show E2B averages 0.747s per execution on CPU workloads: 2.6x slower than self-hosted but 2.7x faster than Modal. For GPU execution, Modal is the better fit. For data residency, self-host via E2B's [open-source infrastructure repo](https://github.com/e2b-dev/infra). For documentation context that helps AI generate accurate infrastructure code, see [Context7 MCP Server](https://www.augmentcode.com/mcp/context7). Augment Code's Context Engine provides similar codebase-aware context, resolving imports across 400,000+ files to generate more accurate code for any execution backend.

## FAQs

### How does E2B's Firecracker microVM isolation differ from Docker container isolation for running AI-generated code?

Firecracker microVMs provide hardware-level isolation with dedicated kernel instances, preventing kernel exploits from escaping to the host. Docker containers share the host kernel through namespaces, making them vulnerable to privilege escalation. For AI-generated code, Firecracker's hypervisor layer blocks malicious outputs from exploiting kernel vulnerabilities at the hardware virtualization boundary that containers cannot enforce.

### How do I configure E2B sandbox timeouts to avoid the silent 60-second default fallback issue?

Explicitly set timeout parameters in both the start and wait methods of your sandbox calls. The silent fallback occurs when you specify timeout in only one location. For example, use \`sandbox.start(timeout=300)\` and \`execution.wait(timeout=300)\` together. If you only set one, the system reverts to sixty seconds regardless of your specified value, causing unexpected terminations during longer operations.

### How do I set up the E2B MCP server with Cursor or VS Code instead of Claude Desktop?

The manual installation method should work: add the JSON configuration snippet to your client's MCP config file with your E2B API key in the env section. For Cursor, check the MCP server settings. For VS Code with GitHub Copilot, enable MCP features first. Neither platform has published E2B-specific documentation, so reference their general MCP integration guides.

### Can MCP servers be customized for specific enterprise applications?

Yes, MCP servers support extensive enterprise customization. Organizations can build custom servers using the protocol specification, creating domain-specific tools, proprietary API integrations, and tailored environments. Open-source implementations allow modification of authentication, compliance logging, data residency enforcement, and internal infrastructure integration. Platforms like E2B enable custom sandbox templates matching enterprise tech stacks.

### Can MCP servers act as proxies for other MCP servers?

Yes, MCP servers can proxy other MCP servers. Projects like MCPJungle operate as unified registries, while AWS MCP Proxy and Databricks provision managed endpoints that bridge clients to backend servers. This proxy pattern centralizes authentication, simplifies multi-server access, and has led to "MCP Gateway" architectures that handle infrastructure complexity across distributed MCP resources.

### What are the best methods to implement strong authentication for MCP servers?

Strong MCP server authentication requires phishing-resistant MFA like FIDO2 security keys or passkeys using hardware-backed cryptography resistant to interception. Enforce Conditional Access policies blocking legacy protocols, apply risk-based step-up authentication via identity protection tools, and replace user-based service accounts with workload identities like managed identities to secure automation without MFA friction. Start with report-only testing to avoid disrupting legacy integrations.
